extraction.name: MMMU
extraction.description: MMMU is a comprehensive benchmark designed to evaluate multimodal models on massive multi-discipline tasks demanding college-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning. It includes 11.5K multimodal questions collected from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks, covering six core disciplines (Art & Design, Business, Science, Health & Medicine, Humanities & Social Science, and Tech & Engineering) across 30 subjects and 183 subfields, comprising 30 heterogeneous image types.
extraction.creator: Xiang Yue, Yuansheng Ni, Kai Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Ruoqi Liu, Ge Zhang, Samuel Stevens, Dongfu Jiang, Weiming Ren, Yuxuan Sun, Cong Wei, Botao Yu, Ruibin Yuan, Renliang Sun, Ming Yin, Boyuan Zheng, Zhenzhu Yang, Yibo Liu, Wenhao Huang, Huan Sun, Yu Su, Wenhu Chen
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data collection took place across three stages. First, common university majors were selected where visual inputs are commonly adopted (ruling out law and linguistics). Second, over 50 university students (including coauthors) collected 13K multimodal questions from textbooks, lecture materials, and online resources, or created new ones based on their expertise, specifically choosing questions without immediately available answers to reduce contamination risks. Third, strict copyright and license avoidance was followed.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: College exams, quizzes, textbooks, lecture materials, and online resources across 30 subjects and 6 core disciplines.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Data cleaning was conducted in two steps: 1) Lexical overlap and source URL similarity were used to identify potential duplicate problems, which were reviewed and eliminated by authors; 2) Problems were distributed among co-authors for format and typo checking to ensure adherence to a standardized format; 3) Categorization into four difficulty levels (very easy, easy, medium, hard), resulting in approximately 10% of problems classified as 'very easy' being excluded.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Questions, multiple-choice options, correct answers, image types, difficulty levels, and optional explanations were annotated into a structured JSON file format following explicit guidelines. Interleaving was handled by inserting image file paths into questions, options, or explanations. Ambiguities were flagged and resolved collaboratively in team meetings, followed by secondary reviews and regular audits.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: A user-friendly web interface developed by Tianyu Zheng for data annotation and verification.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Ambiguities or unclear data instances were flagged for a detailed review process and collaboratively examined in team meetings to establish a standardized annotation approach. Secondary reviews and regular audits of random samples were conducted to ensure sustained quality and consistency.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: A team of over 50 college/university students, including coauthors, specializing in the corresponding 30 subjects across different disciplines.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: A live-updating leaderboard is maintained at https://mmmu-benchmark.github.io/#leaderboard. Specific version change logs detailing updates from V1 through V4 are documented in Appendix J.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Compliance with privacy laws and ethical standards in data handling was maintained; annotators were explicitly instructed to avoid collecting questions that contain any private information.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Provides a benchmark for measuring progress towards Level 3 / Expert AGI ('at least 90th percentile of skilled adults' across diverse domains), which marks a substitution threshold for machine intelligence in lieu of human labor, leading to significant risks of job displacement and economic disruption.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The manual curation process may carry biases. Models evaluated also showed biases, such as prioritizing textual information over visual inputs and certain political beliefs.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: MMMU is not a sufficient test for Expert AGI because there is no direct mapping between benchmark performance and the 90th percentile of skilled adults, nor are college exams the only tasks an AGI must tackle. Additionally, manual curation may carry human biases.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking and evaluating multimodal foundation models and large language models on college-level multi-discipline understanding and deliberate reasoning (testing, validation, few-shot development).
